title: Night walk: the snail-eating glow
storyboard: Film: naturalist on a night walk with a red-filtered torch, finding a glowing firefly larva; hands only

scenes.headline: What's glowing in the leaf litter?
A firefly larva, eating a snail
scenes.body: Firefly larvae inject snails and slugs with fluid, then drink the partly digested meal.

scenes.headline: Light without heat
scenes.body: Fireflies glow by bioluminescence; almost none of the energy is lost as heat.

scenes.headline: Also out tonight: a calling frog
Torch tip: point it at the ground
scenes.body: Never into eyes, never for long. We're guests here.

caption:
The cutest glow on our night walk belongs to a snail hunter.

Firefly light is made when enzymes act on molecules called luciferins, which react with oxygen and ATP.

Source: Britannica, Firefly. Photos/video: Wikimedia Commons (credits on screen).
notes: Storyboard: night-walk shots with the naturalist to be filmed on our nature study camps; CC macro photos stand in. Low-risk, high-trust field format with a surprising fact.
